purpose: Machine-readable inventory and linear-algebra specification for the C(n+1) triviality question

triviality_test_specification.unknown_map: odd f with f(Z_j) = sum_i phi_{ij} Z_i and p(Z_i) = p(Z_j)+1
triviality_test_specification.criterion_for_fixed_gb: vec(gamma_gb) is in the column space of D, where D maps odd-map coefficients phi to vec(delta_f)
triviality_test_specification.equivalent_left_kernel_criterion_when_ga: N^T G gb = 0, where columns of N span the left nullspace of D
triviality_test_specification.global_nonzero_scalar_convention: gamma=lambda*delta_f with one global lambda != 0 is equivalent to gamma=delta_f for some odd f, since delta is linear and lambda can be absorbed into f
triviality_test_specification.scalar_convention_warning: If lambda=0 is allowed, the condition is vacuous; input-dependent or componentwise scalars define a different relation.

missing_inputs_for_numerical_verificatio: A complete homogeneous basis and its parity assignment, matched to the oscillator generators
Complete undeformed structure constants in that basis
Explicit deformed oscillator relations and the resulting coefficients G^r_{ab}(gb)
The coefficient ring and a parity-consistent interpretation of the gb parameters
An explicit nonzero-global-scalar convention if equality is intended only up to scalar

verification_status.reason: The source documents do not specify the data needed to construct these matrices; reporting numerical ranks would fabricate evidence.

conclusion: The supplied definitions do not determine necessary and sufficient conditions on gb or whether nonzero configurations are trivial.
